## Mobile Security Standards

### Secure Local Storage

- **NEVER** store sensitive data (tokens, API keys, PII) in `SharedPreferences`, `NSUserDefaults`, or plain-text files — use platform-backed secure storage (iOS Keychain, Android Keystore).
- Encrypt sensitive database fields with AES-256 — plain SQLite databases are readable on rooted/jailbroken devices.
- Clear all cached credentials and tokens on user logout — **NEVER** leave stale auth data in local storage.

### Authentication & Biometrics

- Use biometric authentication (Face ID, Touch ID, fingerprint) for sensitive actions — always provide a fallback to device PIN/passcode.
- **NEVER** handle raw biometric data — delegate verification to the OS and act only on success/failure callbacks.
- Use OAuth 2.0 / OIDC for session management — **NEVER** implement custom token exchange protocols.

### Network Security

- Enforce HTTPS for all network communication — **NEVER** allow plain HTTP in production builds.
- Implement certificate pinning for high-security APIs (fintech, healthcare) — pin the public key hash, not the certificate itself, to survive certificate rotations.
- Validate and sanitize all server responses before processing — treat API data as untrusted input.

### Code Protection

- Enable code obfuscation for all release builds — **MUST** preserve the debug symbol mapping file for crash report decoding.
- **NEVER** hardcode API keys, secrets, or environment-specific values in source code — inject them at build time or retrieve from a secure backend.
- Implement root/jailbreak detection for apps handling financial or personal data — restrict sensitive features on compromised devices.

> [!WARNING]
> Never log sensitive data (tokens, passwords, PII) even in debug mode — logging frameworks may persist data to disk or crash reporters.
